research_rationale:
Executive Order 12432 of July 14, 1983 (48 FR 32551; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12432.txt, read in full) has two sections. Section 1 requires Federal agencies with substantial procurement or grantmaking authority to develop minority business enterprise development plans, submit them annually to the Cabinet Council on Commerce and Trade, follow uniform guidelines set by the Secretary of Commerce and the Administrator of the Small Business Administration, report annually, and requires the Secretary of Commerce to report annually to the President. Section 2 requires agencies to establish minority business development programs, to encourage grant recipients to achieve minority business participation, and to give the Cabinet Council information on progress. The text states no date, duration, condition or expiry. The packet inventory missed the end of paragraph 2(c) and paragraph 2(d), which print after the Federal Register page break, so the inventory is corrected to ten clauses (inventory overrides). No amendment, revocation or supersession of the order appears in the held Federal Register texts of later orders (a search of the held texts for citations of this order by number found only regulations and rules that implement or cite it), in the Office of the Federal Register catalog (no disposition note), or in the three bounded searches. The eCFR (48 CFR 1426.7100 and 1426.7102-1; 24 CFR 5.105) and the U.S. Code note under 15 U.S.C. 631 treat the order as continuing. The held sources do not show what body now stands in the place of the Cabinet Council on Commerce and Trade, and none says that an end of the Council ended any command of the order; that open point is disclosed in the clauses that name the Council. All ten clauses are operative on 2026-10-14. Standing note on sources: the original is held as a machine text layer of the official Federal Register page; check the page before relying on quotations.
